[
  "When melanoma is suspected, the entire lesion should be completely excised with a narrow margin of 1–3 mm to allow histological diagnosis.",
  "Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as facial lesions (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and genital lesions.",
  "The consensus rate for this recommendation is 100 % (21 out of 21 participants).",
  "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first‑line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness and for melanoma in situ.",
  "Surgical margins should be determined based on tumor thickness.",
  "Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor and, whenever possible, in the same operative setting.",
  "The 5‑point score is driven by pigment network (atypical, 2 points), blue‑whitish veil (present, 2 points), and dots and globules (irregular, 1 point).",
  "Pigment network, blue‑whitish veil, and dots and globules are major or minor features that contribute to melanoma suspicion.",
  "On the image, look for an atypical pigment network characterized by irregular meshes and thickened lines.",
  "On the image, look for a blue‑whitish veil characterized by confluent blue pigment with an overlying white haze.",
  "On the image, look for irregular dots and globules characterized by varied size and uneven distribution."
]
